lines.say: This week, Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are due to hold their first three-way summit, in China.
But in 1945, three leaders met at Yalta and redrew the map of Europe.
In February 1945, with the war nearly won, President Roosevelt flew to Yalta, in Crimea, to meet Churchill and Stalin.
The Big Three sat down to decide the world after the war.
They agreed to divide Germany into zones, and to found the United Nations.
Stalin promised free elections in Poland, and to join the war against Japan.
Poland's borders moved west. Critics said the deal handed Eastern Europe to Stalin.
Now three powers are meeting again, and other countries are watching what they decide.
Should great powers decide other countries' futures?
